question: Old alluvial soil is known as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bangar**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Old alluvial soil is known as Bhangar.
 
• Bhangar is a system of older alluvium that is deposited away from flood plains and forms terraces along river beds that are higher than the floodplain.
 
• Bhangar is not very fertile and is not suitable for agriculture. 
 
• In contrast, newer alluvial soil is called Khadar.
 
• Khadar is more fertile than Bhangar and is used extensively for agriculture.
 
• Khadar is deposited by rivers in their flood plains and is replenished every year. Khadar is also known as Nali or Naili. 
 
• Alluvial soil is made up of clay, gravel, sand, silt, boulders, and other particles, along with organic matter that makes the soil fertile.
 
• Alluvial soil differs in texture because it is a transported soil deposited by rivers.
